meta.note: Single source of truth for the skill exam. Each must_include entry is an independently judged, requested requirement traceable to source. Entries combine with AND; alternatives inside an entry combine with OR and do not require every example. Score uses supported +1, missing 0, incorrect -1, including additional confirmed errors. Minimize errors first; improve coverage concurrently as the second priority. Legacy whole-answer passes are separate. Optional must_not regexes are non-fatal audit hints. Changed banks and rubric granularity are not directly comparable to historical scores.

axes.api: API understanding — signatures, what exists / what was removed
axes.react: Solid vs React — does the model drag React reflexes over
axes.v1: Solid 2.0 vs 1.x — does the model fall back to 1.x APIs

questions.title: createEffect signature
questions.prompt: Describe the `createEffect` form with a function-valued apply callback, including optional arguments: which callbacks track, what may apply return, and how does a one-callback call behave in TypeScript and at runtime in dev? Give a short valid example. Should new code use `createTrackedEffect` instead?
must_include: Use createEffect(compute, apply, options?) for a function-valued apply callback.
The compute callback runs tracked and returns the value passed to apply.
The apply callback runs untracked.
The apply callback may return a cleanup function or undefined, not an assigned string or number.
Include a short valid example of the split compute/apply form.
TypeScript has no one-callback createEffect overload.
A one-callback createEffect call throws synchronously with MISSING_EFFECT_FN in dev.
createTrackedEffect is deprecated migration support; new reactive side effects use split createEffect.

questions.title: reads lag writes
questions.prompt: Given `const [count, setCount] = createSignal(0)`, an event handler calls `setCount(1)`. What does `count()` return on the very next line, and why? How do you force the new value to be readable synchronously?
must_include: The next count() read returns the previously committed value, 0.
Writes commit on a microtask rather than immediately.
flush() drains queued writes synchronously so a subsequent count() reads 1.

questions.title: async data without createResource
questions.prompt: How do you load data asynchronously by id and render it while showing a spinner during loading? Name the primitive and the boundary. Explain whether consumers read a ready value or must check for undefined.
must_include: Use createMemo(() => fetchX(id())) to load async data reactively by id.
Consumers read the resolved value through the memo accessor, not a Promise.
Wrap consumers in a Loading boundary with a spinner fallback.
Loading is structural suspension, not a value consumers must test for undefined.

questions.title: loadingValue and seedLoadingValue
questions.prompt: Contrast `loadingValue` on an async memo with `seedLoadingValue: true` on a derived store. What do consumers, `<Loading>`, and `isPending` observe before the first answer, what happens on later refetches, and how do declared versus bare `ssrSource: "client"` forms render?
must_include: loadingValue supplies an async memo's committed provisional first value.
seedLoadingValue: true exposes a derived store's seed as its committed provisional first value.
Before the first real answer, consumers read the provisional value as settled without suspending Loading.
Before the first real answer, isPending(source) is false for a source with a provisional first value.
After the first answer, the provisional value leaves the lineage; later refetches use ordinary stale-value/pending semantics.
A declared loading/seed value with ssrSource: "client" renders as commit #0 on the server.
The declared loading/seed value also supplies commit #0 through hydration.
A bare ssrSource: "client" source is a structural hole that suspends the nearest Loading boundary.
On the server, a bare client source outside a boundary is a render error.

questions.title: async generator memo — yield vs return
questions.prompt: In a `createMemo(async function* () { … })`, what does each `yield` do to the memo's value, and what does `return value` do? Then contrast `return` here with `return` inside an `action(async function*)`.
must_include: Each async-generator memo yield commits a new accessor value.
An async-generator memo's return ends the stream without committing its return value.
After a memo generator returns, the last yielded value remains.
An async-generator action's return value becomes the action's result.
An action generator's yield is a transaction-safe suspension point, not a committed memo value.

questions.title: uncaught error halts reactivity
questions.prompt: An uncaught reactive error escapes every boundary and the app stops updating. Explain the halt, its proper prevention, and the limits of `resetErrorHalt`: is it exported, what can the production client hook actually reset, what resets automatically in dev, and what does the server export do?
must_include: An error escaping every reactive boundary halts scheduling with REACTIVITY_HALTED.
After a halt, later writes and flushes do not update the app.
Production has no automatic recovery from a reactive halt.
Prevent the halt by handling fallible reactive work in createErrorBoundary or Errored.
resetErrorHalt is re-exported by solid-js as an internal test/dev-reload hook.
The production client resetErrorHalt hook can clear the halt flag.
Clearing the halt flag does not repair a damaged application graph.
Dev render/refresh reset the halt automatically.
The server resetErrorHalt export is a no-op.

questions.title: effect error handler arm
questions.prompt: In `createEffect(compute, { effect, error })`, the `error` handler: (1) can it set a signal to record the message, (2) does it receive the original error object so `instanceof MyError` works, (3) does it catch an exception thrown inside the `effect` (apply) arm? Explain the phase and scope it runs in.
must_include: The error arm runs in an imperative writable effect-phase scope, so setting a signal there is legal.
The error arm is queued on the same schedule as the effect arm.
The error arm receives the original error, preserving identity and instanceof checks.
The error arm handles compute errors, including async source rejections.
An exception in the effect/apply arm bypasses this error arm and reaches the enclosing error boundary.

questions.title: async-gen action uncaught error + resolve rejection
questions.prompt: Inside an `action(async function* () { … })`, an awaited server call rejects and nothing catches it. Does the app freeze? What happens to the returned promise and to the optimistic writes? Separately: if you `await resolve(() => user())` and the underlying source rejected, what do you get back? Can the rejection be handled inside the generator, and what happens to optimistic writes if it catches and then completes successfully?
must_include: An uncaught action-generator error rejects the returned Promise.
The failed action completes the transition and reverts its optimistic writes.
An action rejection does not halt app reactivity.
try/catch around yield/await can handle the rejection inside the generator.
Successful completion also removes optimistic overlays; catching the error does not make those writes permanent.
resolve(() => user()) rejects with the source's own error when user rejected.

questions.title: action invocation scope guard
questions.prompt: A component defines `const save = action(async function* () { await api.save(); yield; setSaved(true); })` and then calls `save()` directly in the component body (or from a memo compute). Is that legal? Where should the call live, and what failure is the guard preventing?
must_include: Defining an action in component setup is legal.
Invoking an action synchronously in an owned setup/compute scope throws ACTION_CALLED_IN_OWNED_SCOPE in dev.
Invoke the action in an imperative scope, such as an event handler or an effect apply/error callback.
Starting an action is a transaction-starting write.
The guard prevents a computation from repeatedly starting replacement transitions in response to its own writes, causing livelock.

questions.title: falsy error identity and nested boundaries
questions.prompt: What values reach user code for `Promise.reject(null)` under `<Errored>` / an effect `error` arm, and for an action generator that `throw undefined` — does the returned action Promise resolve or reject? Also, an inner Errored is inside Loading, which is inside an outer Errored: which boundary catches an error from the inner content?
must_include: Promise.reject(null) reaches Errored's err() as null rather than an internal wrapper.
Promise.reject(null) reaches an effect error arm as null rather than an internal wrapper.
An action generator throwing undefined rejects its Promise with undefined; it does not resolve successfully.
The inner Errored catches its content's error through the intervening Loading boundary.

questions.title: empty async iterator settlement
questions.prompt: A memo uses `createMemo(async function* () { return finalValue; })` and never yields. Does its `<Loading>` fallback stay forever, and does `finalValue` become the memo value? What should the generator do to publish a final value?
must_include: A memo iterator that completes without yielding settles its value to undefined.
That empty iterator completion releases Loading.
The memo generator's return value is discarded.
Publish a final memo value with yield finalValue.

questions.title: createReaction re-arm replacement
questions.prompt: For `const track = createReaction(cb); track(() => a()); track(() => b());`, both track calls happen before either source changes. What happens when `a` changes and then `b` changes? Is the reaction persistent, and how is it armed for another cycle?
must_include: The second track call replaces the first arm, so changing a does not call cb.
Changing b calls cb once.
The reaction disarms after that invalidation rather than persisting.
Call track again to arm the next cycle.

questions.title: affects(target, key?) signature and semantics
questions.prompt: What does `affects(target, key?)` do, and what is its exact signature? Can you call `affects(state, "user", "name")` to mark one nested slot two levels deep? Does marking a store with `affects(store)` cover records added to it after the call?
must_include: affects(target, key?) accepts an accessor/Store target and at most one optional key.
affects(record, key) marks exactly that named slot.
affects(store) marks all records reachable at the time of the call.
affects(state, "user", "name") is an invalid three-argument call, not a nested path.
Mark a nested slot by targeting its record.
Records added after affects(store) are not covered by that mark.

questions.title: server function validation follows directive placement
questions.prompt: You write `export const getUser = withValidation(userIdSchema, async (id) => { "use server"; return db.users.find(id); })`, hoping `withValidation` rejects bad ids before the function body runs. Does that work? Why or why not, and where must the check actually live? Also contrast wrapping an export in a module-level `use server` file. Explain which code reaches the client and whether TypeScript argument types provide runtime protection.
must_include: A function-level use server directive registers the raw inner function for HTTP dispatch.
Wrapping that function reference does not put the outer validation wrapper on the HTTP dispatch path.
Put validation/authentication inside the function-level server function.
TypeScript argument types do not validate decoded arguments at runtime.
A module-level use server file registers the exported evaluated function value, including its userland wrapper.
A module-level exported wrapper runs for HTTP and direct calls.
Client output contains bare references; schemas, wrappers, and server dependencies remain server-side.

questions.title: server function metadata: .GET / .withOptions removed
questions.prompt: Can you read `getUser.GET` or call `getUser.withOptions({...})` on a server function reference? Show the supported declaration, metadata inspection, and session transport APIs. Include allowed HTTP methods/status for undeclared GET, metadata composition across bundles, wrapper/compiler requirements, and rotating auth headers.
must_include: Server function references have no .GET proxy getter.
Server function references have no .withOptions(init) method.
GET(fn) declares GET support.
withMeta(fn, metadata) shallow-merges metadata.
GET and withMeta compose in either order.
The function-level compiler transform preserves these runtime wrapper calls; no special wrapper transform is required.
GET(fn) keeps POST accepted.
GET on a function without GET declaration is rejected with 405.
Inspect metadata with getServerFunctionMetadata/isServerFunction using registered-symbol brands rather than property sniffing.
Rotating auth headers belong in the client session prepareRequest hook, not declaration metadata.
prepareRequest runs before each outgoing call.

questions.title: respond/redirect/reload and isResponseEnvelope
questions.prompt: A login server function does `if (bad) return respond({ error: 'bad' }, { status: 401 }); return redirect('/dashboard');`. What do `respond`/`redirect`/`reload` actually return? Distinguish ordinary Responses from envelopes, explain how to detect envelopes across bundles, and name the exact revalidation header and its exported constant.
must_include: respond(value, init?) returns a ResponseEnvelope pairing an in-memory value with HTTP metadata.
redirect(url, init?) returns an ordinary Response, not a ResponseEnvelope.
redirect defaults to status 302.
reload(init?) returns an empty-body Response with revalidation metadata, not a ResponseEnvelope.
Detect envelopes with isResponseEnvelope(value).
instanceof ResponseEnvelope is unreliable across separately bundled copies.
The registered-symbol envelope brand survives those bundle boundaries.
Import REVALIDATE_HEADER from root @solidjs/web rather than hard-coding the revalidation header name.
REVALIDATE_HEADER names the X-Revalidate header.

questions.title: affects() called outside an action does nothing visible
questions.prompt: I call `affects(todos)` from a plain click handler (no `action()` wrapping it) right before kicking off a fetch, expecting the list to read pending while the fetch runs. `isPending(() => todos.length)` never flips in the UI. Why, and where does `affects` belong?
must_include: An affects mark outside an action/transaction expires at the end of the current flush.
That short-lived mark never reaches effects or the UI as pending state.
Place affects inside an action alongside its work so the mark lasts until the transaction settles or reverts.

questions.title: reconcile default-id and positional modes
questions.prompt: What is the exact second argument of `reconcile(value, ...)`? Explain omitted, `null`, and missing-key behavior, plus what happens for an array/object shape mismatch and for a different root entity selected by the caller.
must_include: reconcile(value, key?) takes a string, key extractor, or null as key, not a v1 options object.
Omitting key selects the id property.
key: null selects positional merging.
An item missing the selected key falls back to positional matching.
A nested array/object shape mismatch replaces the slot.
Standalone reconcile throws when asked to merge a different root entity into the caller-selected slot.

questions.title: store shallow option overloads
questions.prompt: Importing from solid-js, which plain and derived createStore/createOptimisticStore overloads accept shallow options? What are their option types and are derived optimistic stores refreshable? Can a derived callback mutate its draft without returning data? Show its return type.
must_include: Plain createStore(initial, options?) accepts StoreOptions with shallow.
Plain createOptimisticStore(initial, options?) accepts StoreOptions with shallow.
Plain StoreOptions contains name and shallow; hydration options belong to the derived ProjectionOptions instead.
Derived createStore takes derive, seed, and ProjectionOptions.
Derived createOptimisticStore takes derive, seed, and ProjectionOptions.
ProjectionOptions includes key and shallow.
Derived optimistic stores are refreshable.
The derive callback permits void, T, Promise<void | T>, or AsyncIterable<void | T>, including mutation without a returned value.

questions.title: recursive JSX refs and applyRef typing
questions.prompt: A renderer library forwards nested Solid DOM refs. What shapes does `JSX.Ref<T>` allow, what is the generic `applyRef` signature, and which argument determines the concrete DOM element subtype? Explain the callback-inference constraint and the idiomatic way for the library to apply refs.
must_include: JSX.Ref<T> accepts a direct T.
JSX.Ref<T> accepts a RefCallback<T>.
JSX.Ref<T> accepts undefined.
JSX.Ref<T> accepts arrays of Ref<T>, recursively including nested arrays.
applyRef<T extends Element = Element> takes a callback or flat array of callbacks, an element: T, and returns void.
applyRef's callback element parameter uses NoInfer<T>.
The actual element argument determines the concrete T.
NoInfer prevents callback annotations from choosing or widening T.
Renderer library code should apply refs with applyRef.

questions.title: claimElementTree is integration-only
questions.prompt: Should application code call `claimElementTree(root)` as a normal ref/hydration helper? What does Solid use it for, what descendants are claimed, and what does its server export do?
must_include: claimElementTree is renderer/integration infrastructure, not an application ref or hydration helper.
On the client it claims navigation-relevant descendants such as a[href] and form[action] when DOM arrives without compiled creation code.
The server claimElementTree export is a no-op.

questions.title: built-in no-JS flash and redirect protocol
questions.prompt: A browser submits a Solid server-function form with JavaScript disabled. What does core do by default with truthy and falsy ordinary returned/thrown outcomes versus a returned/thrown `Response`, where does it redirect, and how can an integration replay or disable this behavior? Include helper export locations, async decoding/cleanup, cookie secrecy and size limits. Which request properties select this convention, and can a direct HTTP caller trigger it too?
must_include: createNoJSHandler flashes ordinary non-Response returned/thrown outcomes, including 0, false, empty string, and null.
undefined redirects without creating a flash outcome.
Ordinary no-JS outcomes redirect with 303.
The redirect goes to referer, falling back to configured base or /.
A returned/thrown Response is not flashed.
A Response outcome preserves its headers.
A Response outcome preserves Location and a valid redirect status.
A Response outcome without Location redirects back.
FLASH_COOKIE, hasFlashCookie, and clearFlashCookie come from the isomorphic @solidjs/web/server-functions entry.
encodeFlashCookie, decodeFlashCookie, and createNoJSHandler come from @solidjs/web/server-functions/server.
Clear the flash cookie on the following render even when decoding fails.
A custom handleNoJS can change the form convention.
Per-request handleNoJS overrides take priority.
Server handleNoJS: null disables the convention.
Flash payloads have a roughly 4 KB ceiling.
Oversized outcomes may degrade to truncated: true, which should render as bounded status.
Flash is AES-GCM encrypted.
Use a deployment secret, with a bundler-injected secret as fallback.
Without either secret, withhold the flash outcome while still redirecting.
encodeFlashCookie is asynchronous.
Await asynchronous decodeFlashCookie.
Invalid/tampered cookies decode as no flash.
The default convention matches an untagged form POST to the bare address with Sec-Fetch-Mode absent or navigate, including matching direct HTTP requests.
A non-navigation fetch mode on that untagged form POST is rejected with 400.
Scripted or tagged direct HTTP calls keep their response protocol.

questions.title: server-function transport integration seams
questions.prompt: An integration must send Date/Map arguments and consume a custom response/single-flight envelope. What is the standard rich-argument opt-in, which client hooks consume custom responses, is `codec` alone enough, what does `decodeResponsePayload` return, which server-side transform hooks mirror the integration, and what complete set of fields does `ServerFunctionOutcome` provide?
must_include: Enable Date/Map arguments with enableRichArguments() from @solidjs/web/server-functions/rich-args.
That opt-in installs serializeArgs; codec alone does not supply the rich argument encoder.
responseHandler.capture runs synchronously at the call site.
responseHandler.handle receives the response before normal decoding.
A non-undefined handle return becomes the call result.
decodeResponsePayload(response) returns { value, flightData? }.
Server transformResult handles transport outcomes.
Server transformDirectResult handles in-process outcomes.
ServerFunctionOutcome includes id.
ServerFunctionOutcome includes value.
ServerFunctionOutcome includes response.
ServerFunctionOutcome includes request.
ServerFunctionOutcome includes thrown.
ServerFunctionOutcome includes targetUrl.
ServerFunctionOutcome includes revalidateKeys.
ServerFunctionOutcome includes foldedHeaders.

questions.title: experimental frames surface and stability
questions.prompt: Are Solid server components part of the stable 2.0 contract? Which package subpaths contain the client/server frame APIs, and name the key client and server integration exports without using the retired marker-range APIs.
must_include: Server components are an experimental preview outside Solid 2.0 stability guarantees.
Pin server-component package versions.
The conditional frame entry is @solidjs/web/frames.
Explicit client frame APIs live at @solidjs/web/frames/client.
Explicit server frame APIs live at @solidjs/web/frames/server.

Name a current client integration export, such as installServerComponents, createFrameHost, createFrameElement, applyFrameResponse, or isFrameStreamResponse; these are alternatives, not an exhaustive required list.

Name a current server integration export, such as renderServerComponent, serverComponentResponse, frameTransformResult, or frameTransformDirectResult; these are alternatives, not an exhaustive required list.

questions.title: Promise of AsyncIterable flattening
questions.prompt: A server function returns `Promise<AsyncIterable<Message>>`, and a memo returns that promise directly. Does the memo settle to the iterable object, or stream it? Is a `yield* await serverFn()` adapter required?
must_include: Solid flattens Promise<AsyncIterable> into one streaming computation rather than settling to the iterable object.
Each yielded item becomes a committed memo value.
A yield* await adapter is not required.

questions.title: fully settled SSR string
questions.prompt: How do you obtain a fully settled async HTML string in @solidjs/web 2.0 rc.8? Does `renderToStringAsync` exist, and can you also pipe/read the same render after awaiting it?
must_include: renderToStringAsync does not exist in this version.
await renderToStream(code, options) uses its PromiseLike<string> result to obtain fully settled HTML.
A render has one consumer: choose await, pipe, pipeTo, or readable; mixing distinct consumers throws.

questions.title: server-function security defaults
questions.prompt: What happens to a plain Error thrown by a production server function, how do you intentionally expose a safe client-facing error, and what same-origin/CSRF protection does the handler apply by default? What selects development versus production policy, and how should an integration recognize intentionally safe errors?
must_include: A production plain Error is sanitized to Error("Internal Server Error") without its original message, stack, or own properties.
The build variant, not NODE_ENV, selects development versus production error policy.
Expose intentional client-facing error content through a response envelope or markSafeError(error) from @solidjs/web.
Recognize intentionally safe errors across bundles with isSafeError.
Server-function HTTP handlers enable same-origin CSRF protection by default.

questions.title: server setter writes are deprecated
questions.prompt: During SSR, code writes a signal, a store, and an optimistic store from subscription callbacks. What happens today, and what model should replace those writes?
must_include: SSR setters warn with SERVER_WRITE once per process/category.
SSR signal and store writes only change inert data for later reads/serialization.
SSR signal and store writes do not re-render.
SSR optimistic writes are no-ops; their setter callback does not run.
Represent server changes as async computation sources, such as a subscription returned as an AsyncIterable.

questions.title: diagnostics harness
questions.prompt: For an automated reactivity regression test, what published package captures structured diagnostics and recompute budgets instead of scraping console output? Name the core capture helper and representative assertions. Show a small healthy-scenario capture example with a numeric rerun budget filtered by scope, including ownership and disposal of the test graph, and contrast it with a test deliberately triggering a warning. Which root export exposes the raw diagnostics channel, and in which build conditions is it available?
must_include: Use @solidjs/diagnostics with captureArtifact() to capture structured diagnostics/attribution.
Name a diagnostic assertion such as expectDiagnostic or expectNoDiagnostics; either satisfies this requirement.
Name a recompute/waste budget assertion such as expectRerunBudget or expectNoWaste; either satisfies this requirement.
Obtain artifact from captureArtifact and pass a numeric maximum plus an optional scope filter to expectRerunBudget(artifact, max, options).
OBSERVE from solid-js exposes diagnostics in development/observe builds; it is absent in ordinary production.
Use expectNoDiagnostics for the healthy capture and expectDiagnostic for a separate deliberate-warning capture; these assertions do not consume events.
Drive the healthy scenario's writes from an imperative scope, outside owned root setup/computations.
Dispose the test graph when the scenario completes.

questions.title: RequestEventLocals module augmentation
questions.prompt: How should an app type custom `getRequestEvent()!.locals.user` data in Solid 2.0, and what declaration-file shape accidentally replaces package types instead of augmenting them?
must_include: Augment RequestEventLocals in declare module "@solidjs/web" to type RequestEvent.locals.
Make the declaration file a module with a top-level import or export {}.
A global script-style declare module replaces/defines the ambient module rather than augmenting the package.

questions.title: measure-then-position (createRenderEffect)
questions.prompt: You portal a tooltip panel into document.body and must measure it with getBoundingClientRect() then set its top/left. Which effect do you use, and where do you read the geometry — inside the `ref` callback or somewhere else? Why is the measurement correct?
must_include: Use createRenderEffect for measure-then-write layout.
Read geometry after insertion, not directly in a potentially pre-insertion ref callback; a signal ref tracked by the render effect is one valid approach.
Post-insertion measurement observes the inserted portaled node's geometry.

questions.title: paint timing — no flash
questions.prompt: A tooltip panel is portaled into document.body. An effect measures its inserted DOM node and sets its position. If you use createEffect instead of createRenderEffect, does that choice itself cause a visible flash at the wrong position? Explain the paint timing precisely, and give the real reason to prefer the render lane.
must_include: Choosing createEffect instead of createRenderEffect does not itself cause a visible positioning flash.
Render and user effects run in the same microtask flush before browser paint.
Solid createEffect is not a React-style post-paint phase.
The render lane keeps layout work ordered with DOM work and before user-lane consumers.
Render-lane work is not deferred by Suspense/hydration as user-lane work can be.

questions.title: list rendering with For
questions.prompt: Render a list of todos keyed by identity. Then show how you would render it index-keyed (the old <Index> behavior). Include the typed collection source and imports, and note the callback shapes.
must_include: Use For with default/keyed=true for identity-keyed rows.
Pass an array value to For each; invoke a collection accessor if that is the chosen source type.
Identity-keyed For passes a raw item to its callback.
Identity-keyed For passes an index accessor, read as i().
Use For keyed=false for index-keyed rows.
Index-keyed For passes an item accessor, read as item().
Index-keyed For passes a plain numeric index.

questions.title: store nested update
questions.prompt: Update a nested store field `user.name` and push a string item to an initially empty `list` in one store. Show a strict-TypeScript-compatible example with the import and the setter call.
must_include: Import createStore from solid-js, not the removed solid-js/store subpath.
Update user.name by mutating it inside the store setter's draft callback.
Push into list inside the store setter's draft callback.
The initially empty list accepts string items under strict TypeScript rather than being inferred as never[].
Draft mutation is the default setter behavior; no produce import/wrapper is needed.
A setter mutation callback returns void, or an intentional replacement root, not the numeric result of Array.push.

questions.title: cancel an in-flight fetch on re-run
questions.prompt: A memo `createMemo(async () => fetchUser(id()))` re-runs when `id()` changes. Does Solid cancel the previous in-flight request for you? Show how to abort it on a re-run and on dispose.
must_include: Solid discards a superseded result but does not automatically cancel the in-flight request.
Create an AbortController in the memo computation.
Register onCleanup(() => controller.abort()) synchronously before suspension.
Pass the controller's signal to fetch.
The registered cancellation aborts on rerun and on disposal.

questions.title: stream a socket through an async-gen memo and clean it up
questions.prompt: Stream messages from a WebSocket through `createMemo(async function* () { … })` so each message updates the accessor. How do you tear the socket down on dispose, and why isn't a `try/finally` inside the generator enough? Explain what Solid does to the iterator and what happens to ownership after suspension. Include the push-to-iterator bridge implementation.
must_include: Each yielded socket message commits as the memo's value.
Register onCleanup synchronously before the first await/yield.
Owner context is absent after suspension.
Cleanup actively closes/cancels the socket subscription.
Cleanup also unblocks the parked await so the generator can unwind.
Solid calls return() on the iterator during disposal.
A generator's return() queues behind a parked external await, so try/finally alone cannot reliably tear down a silent socket.
The push bridge drains messages arriving during a yield before parking for another message.

questions.title: bare refresh() is a silent same-question re-ask; optimistic writes are verdict-inert
questions.prompt: An action does an optimistic `createOptimisticStore` write, then `yield`s the server call, then `refresh(todos)`. You try to show a `Saving…` spinner with `<Show when={isPending(() => todos.length)}>` — but it never appears. Why doesn't isPending report the in-flight save, and how do you show the saving state correctly?
must_include: An optimistic write is verdict-inert: its slot does not become pending from the write.
An optimistic write does not mask other pending sources.
A bare same-key refresh is quiet and does not itself make isPending true.
Show the save process through data read by value, such as a co-written optimistic pending field or a separate createOptimistic flag; these are alternative implementations, not a required pair.

questions.title: onSettled cleanup only in an owned scope
questions.prompt: Inside an event handler (not the component body) you call `onSettled(() => { const off = subscribe(); return () => off(); })`. Does that returned cleanup run, and where should setup-with-teardown live instead?
must_include: An event-handler onSettled call has no owner for its returned cleanup.
Returning that unowned cleanup throws SETTLED_CLEANUP_UNOWNED in dev.
Production drops that unowned cleanup.
Keep setup-with-teardown owned by component/root setup: component-body onSettled returning cleanup, or direct owned subscription setup plus onCleanup are valid alternatives.

questions.title: store-in-store structural tracking
questions.prompt: A derived store wraps an inner store and For renders outer.items. Compare subscriptions for For/mapArray (show their collection arguments), Object.keys(outer) versus Object.keys(outer.items), deep, direct field reads, and a memo that only calls snapshot. After inner reconcile/add/delete, what stays current, and should the inner store be cloned?
must_include: For/mapArray track structural changes through the outer wrapper.
For each takes outer.items directly; mapArray takes a list accessor such as () => outer.items.
Object.keys(outer.items) tracks inner structural changes through the wrapper.
Object.keys(outer) tracks only outer keys, not additions/deletions inside outer.items.
deep tracks structural changes through the wrapper.
Inner reconcile/add/delete changes reach those structural consumers.
Direct field reads subscribe to their respective fields.
snapshot reads current inner data without subscribing.
A memo that only calls snapshot does not rerun for inner writes.
Preserve the inner proxy instead of cloning it to retain the fine-grained live view.

questions.title: lazy SSR identity and hydration
questions.prompt: An SSR app creates a lazy component from an `import.meta.glob` entry, so the `lazy()` callsite has no static `moduleUrl`.
